provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: Every empty cell starts with colour palette[0], and every seed cell has colour palette[1]. The emitted program floods from all seed cells in the visible grid. It recolours any empty cell that is orthogonally (4-way) connected to a seed through other empty cells, including cells already filled by the flood. This is exactly what the constructor does: it pops blue cells and recolours orthogonal neighbours that are still black. It is the same as the archived solver's rule: fill every 4-connected background component that touches an original seed orthogonally. 4-adjacency, grid bounds and connectivity are all invariant under the eight D4 transforms, so no axis or direction needs to be specialised. Only the two colour roles are specialised, as palette[0] and palette[1]. The program works on rectangular grids, and it handles components touching the border and seeds at the border by plain bounds checks. Seeds that are adjacent to each other or that share one region raise no tie issues, because the flood result does not depend on processing order.
draft_notes.limitations: The program assumes the episode keeps the constructor's colour roles: background is palette[0] and seed/fill is palette[1]. It does not infer these roles from the demonstrations. I found no constructor defects or hidden random tie-breaks. The result is order-independent, and the fixtures match the uniform rule. The constructor only builds square grids, but the emitted program also handles rectangular ones. I have not run any tests.
